title: Tesla Model X collision with crash attenuator in Mountain View
system_purpose: Partial driving automation supported steering and longitudinal speed control.
decision_impact: Autosteer and Traffic-Aware Cruise Control influenced lane path and vehicle speed.
affected_groups: Tesla driver; occupants and other road users; road-safety operators
verified_facts: NTSB reported that the Tesla was using Traffic-Aware Cruise Control and Autosteer when it entered a highway gore area and struck a crash attenuator. NTSB identified system limitations, driver non-response and ineffective driver-engagement monitoring as causal or contributing factors.
reported_harm: The Tesla driver died after the collision; two other vehicles were involved, one driver had minor injuries and one was uninjured.
quantitative_evidence: The vehicle struck the attenuator at about 71 mph on March 23, 2018; the crash involved two subsequent vehicle collisions.
limitations: The case includes a damaged crash attenuator and roadway-maintenance factors, so the outcome cannot be attributed only to the ADAS. It is one investigation and not a population-level performance estimate.

title: Tesla Autosteer recall for insufficient misuse controls
system_purpose: Level 2 driver assistance provided steering support while the driver remained responsible.
decision_impact: Autosteer controls affected whether drivers recognized system status and stayed prepared to intervene.
affected_groups: Tesla drivers; vehicle occupants; other road users; vehicle manufacturer and safety reviewers
verified_facts: NHTSA acknowledged a recall covering Tesla vehicles equipped with affected Autosteer versions because the prominence and scope of controls might not sufficiently prevent driver misuse. The notice states that an unprepared driver may face increased crash risk.
reported_harm: The notice describes a foreseeable safety hazard from misuse and automation disengagement; it does not claim that every affected vehicle experienced a crash.
quantitative_evidence: The recall covered an estimated 2,031,220 vehicles, and NHTSA stated that its investigation reviewed 956 reported crashes before focusing on 322 Autopilot-involved crashes.
limitations: The recall notice does not establish that all reviewed crashes were caused by Autosteer controls, and it does not by itself demonstrate the effectiveness of the software remedy.
